P2: status on the epoch/respawn job — in progress, not blocked, coordinating with P4.

FINDING: the destructive PtyHostService.spawn() replace path (the one that actually mints a
new epoch) has NO reachable trigger through the real catalog today. execution.spawn always
creates a new work_session/sessionId; SpawnService.spawn() only ever calls the
reattach-safe pty.spawnIfAbsent(); reconcileNodeGhosts() explicitly skips sessions with a
live PTY. I greped every caller — nothing in the current wiring calls the destructive branch
twice for one sessionId. So I can't exercise this from the browser or via curl against the
shared :4610 node the way I've tested everything else.

Also, per the new governance rule, I can't construct PtyHostService directly myself by
adding a file to packages/server/test/ or packages/execution/src — that's brokered
territory, and it's genuinely P4's lane this session anyway.

WHAT'S ALREADY PROVEN (so this isn't starting from zero): the CLIENT-SIDE algorithm is
already unit-tested against exactly an epoch change, with a simulated frame sequence, in
ptyTransport.test.ts:125 ("RESETS when the epoch changes (a respawn), even without a byte
rewind") — real product code, `_handleAttached`, just driven by a FakeWebSocket rather than
a real server. So the remaining gap is narrow and specific: does the REAL PtyHostService +
pty-ws-server actually produce that transition faithfully (different epoch, close-without-
exit, coherent replay) when a real process gets replaced.

ACTION TAKEN: sent P4 a concrete split proposal — they extend their existing
pty-ws.test.ts-style harness (host.spawn() called twice on one sessionId, exactly the shape
their file already has for everything else) to capture the raw-wire evidence, since that's

through my terminal-dev.html harness if they can give me a real reachable URL for it — that

Will report the observation (not adjectives) once P4 responds or gives me a port to test
